Definition: from G575 and G2875; to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts):--cut off. Compare G2699.
BiblicalUsage: To cut off, to amputate. Jesus commands it twice in Mark 9:43 and Mark 9:45 — if thy hand offend thee, cut it off; if thy foot offend thee, cut it off — better maimed entering into life than whole into hell. Peter does it literally in John 18:10, cutting off the high priest's servant's right ear, and Paul wishes it on the troublers in Galatians 5:12: I would they were even cut off which trouble you.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Jesus' command is not about the hand; it is about how seriously I take the sin the hand serves. Better to lose the thing I love than to keep it and lose life. Peter's sword shows the wrong cutting — violence against another man — while Paul's wish shows the right one: the troublers cut off from the church, so the flock is safe.
